title: Predicting Short-term Survival after Liver Transplantation using Machine Learning
summary: Magnesium appeared among the leading selected features alongside INR, lymphocytes, platelets, WBC, sodium, age and BMI. The random-forest model achieved temporal-validation AUC 0.771, specificity 0.815 and sensitivity 0.50, outperforming the compared models by AUC. Derivation: 480 patients from 2004–2012 with 10-fold cross-validation. Temporal validation: 58 patients from 2013, including four deaths. This is existing-data temporal validation, not external validation; the small event count and lack of external testing limit generalizability. The article states external validation remains future work.
ai_technology: Random forest selected candidate predictors and produced the 30-day postoperative survival model from preoperative measurements; the source reports feature importance and compares the model with XGBoost, decision tree and logistic regression.
